title: Key characteristics of the agile mindset
blurb: Define the key characteristics of the agile mindset and recognize each one in a team's behaviour.
question: A team is given the freedom to decide how it delivers its work. Which characteristic of the agile mindset does this reflect?

teach.h: What the mindset looks like in behaviour
teach.body: The agile mindset is a way of thinking, so how do you spot it? PRINCE2 Agile describes key characteristics that show up in how people behave. Those the book explains include collaboration, transparency and rich communication, respect, empowerment and adaptability. Each one has a recognizable anchor phrase, and exam questions usually describe a behaviour and ask which characteristic it shows.

teach.h: Five characteristics the book explains: CREAT
Anchor phrases to recognize each one
head: Characteristic
Anchor phrase
You see it when
rows: The team decides how to work
Every voice is heard and valued
The team changes course on evidence
Users and team shape solutions together

teach.body: Empowerment fosters autonomy and self-management within teams: whenever a stem mentions freedom to make decisions, think empowerment. Respect is rooted in empathy and open-mindedness. All voices are valued, diverse perspectives are embraced, and each member's contribution is acknowledged. Empathy helps people understand each other; open-mindedness means listening to new ideas without bias, so everyone feels able to share.

Adaptability reflects the agile values of inspection and adaptation in response to change. Transparency and rich communication mean information flows openly and is more than just text; regular meetings, open documentation and visible work status build trust and keep everyone aligned, and people share obstacles without fear. Collaboration means working closely with team members, stakeholders and users, with a culture of shared ownership and mutual support that leads to co-created solutions.

teach.h: Which characteristic is the stem describing?

root.label: Read the behaviour in the stem

rows.label: Stand-ups
values: Members drop in as they like

teach.body: Glenmoor Rail is building a staff rostering app. Team coach Callum Fraser notices three things. Two developers skip the daily stand-up and email updates instead, so blockers surface late: he asks everyone to attend and moves the burn chart onto a shared screen (transparency). Retrospectives are dominated by senior staff: he runs a format where each person speaks in turn (respect). The product owner agrees boundaries within which the team chooses its own approach (empowerment).

teach.text: Freedom to make decisions is empowerment, not respect or transparency. Respect is about empathy and open-mindedness so that every voice is heard; transparency is about open, rich information flow. Exams use these three as distractors for each other.

items: Empowerment: autonomy and self-management within teams.
Respect: empathy and open-mindedness; all voices valued.
Adaptability: inspection and adaptation in response to change.
Transparency and rich communication: open information flow, more than text; visible work status.
Collaboration: working closely with team, stakeholders and users; shared ownership and co-creation.

summary: You can now define the agile mindset characteristics the book describes: collaboration, transparency and rich communication, respect, empowerment and adaptability. You can also match a described behaviour to the right characteristic using its anchor phrase.

A.q: Which characteristic of the agile mindset fosters autonomy and self-management within teams?
A.why: Empowerment fosters autonomy and self-management within teams (2.6.2).

whyNot.0: Respect is rooted in empathy and open-mindedness.
whyNot.1: Adaptability concerns inspection and adaptation in response to change.
whyNot.3: Transparency concerns open, rich communication and visible work.

A.q: According to PRINCE2 Agile, the agile characteristic of respect is rooted in what?
A.why: Respect is rooted in empathy and open-mindedness, so that all voices are valued (2.6.2).

whyNot.3: Visible work and open documentation support transparency.

A.q: Which characteristic of the agile mindset reflects the agile values of inspection and adaptation in response to change?
A.why: Adaptability reflects inspection and adaptation in response to change (2.6.2).

whyNot.0: Collaboration is about shared ownership and co-creating solutions.
whyNot.1: Respect is about empathy, open-mindedness and valuing all voices.
whyNot.2: Empowerment is about autonomy and self-management.

B.q: Two team members often skip the daily stand-up and send written updates later, so blockers are found late. Which action best supports transparency and rich communication?
options: Let them attend on the days they prefer
Ask the whole team to attend and show work visibly
Have the project manager present their progress
Set up a separate stand-up for the two of them
B.why: Transparency relies on regular meetings, open documentation and visible work status, with information that is more than just text (2.6.2).

whyNot.0: Optional attendance keeps information patchy and blockers hidden.
whyNot.2: Someone else presenting progress does not open up information sharing within the team.
whyNot.3: Separate stand-ups split the team's information flow instead of making it open.

B.q: Users, stakeholders and the delivery team work side by side and design a solution together, each feeling ownership of it. Which characteristic of the agile mindset does this show?
B.why: Collaboration means working closely with team members, stakeholders and users, with shared ownership that leads to co-created solutions (2.6.2).

whyNot.0: Empowerment is about the team's autonomy and self-management.
whyNot.1: Adaptability is about inspecting and adapting to change.
whyNot.3: Respect is about empathy and valuing all voices, not joint design.

B.q: A coach plans a session on new ways of working for a team spread across two sites. Which option best reflects the agile characteristic of respect?
options: A virtual session the whole team joins
An in-person session for key members
An online course people take alone
One-to-one sessions with the most senior staff
B.why: Respect means all voices are valued and diverse perspectives embraced; a session the whole team can join lets everyone be heard (2.6.2).

whyNot.1: Limiting attendance to key members leaves other voices out.
whyNot.2: Solo online learning does not let team members hear and value each other.
whyNot.3: Sessions with senior staff leave most of the team unheard.

C.q:
Which two statements about the characteristics of the agile mindset are correct?
1. Empowerment fosters autonomy and self-management.
2. Transparency means producing comprehensive written reports.
3. Respect is rooted in empathy and open-mindedness.
4. Adaptability means following the agreed process without deviation.
C.why: Empowerment fosters autonomy and self-management (1), and respect is rooted in empathy and open-mindedness (3) (2.6.2).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: transparency is open information flow that is more than just text.
whyNot.2: Both are wrong: transparency is not about written reports and adaptability is about changing in response to inspection.
whyNot.3: Statement 4 is wrong: adaptability is inspection and adaptation, not rigid process-following.

C.q: At Ferncastle Libraries, the product owner agrees boundaries with the team and then lets the team choose how to deliver each iteration. Which characteristic is shown, and why?
options: Respect, because every voice is heard
Adaptability, because the plan has been changed
C.why: Letting the team decide within agreed boundaries fosters autonomy and self-management, which is empowerment (2.6.2).

whyNot.0: Respect concerns empathy and valuing voices; the stem is about freedom to decide.
whyNot.1: The stem says nothing about making work visible; it is about decision freedom.
whyNot.2: No change of plan is described; the team has been given autonomy.

C.q: A team's board shows every blocker, and members raise problems early without fear of blame. Which characteristic is this, and what does it build?
options: Transparency, which builds trust and alignment
C.why: Open information flow and visible work status are transparency, which builds trust and keeps everyone aligned on goals, progress and challenges (2.6.2).

whyNot.0: Respect is about empathy and open-mindedness; autonomy belongs to empowerment.
whyNot.2: Empowerment is about autonomy and self-management, not visibility.
whyNot.3: Adaptability is about inspecting and adapting; shared ownership belongs to collaboration.

reteach.title: Five signals on the team wall
reteach.question: How do you tell the characteristics apart quickly?

blocks.h: Ask what the behaviour is about
blocks.body: Ask one question: what is this behaviour mainly about? Deciding for ourselves: empowerment. Everyone being heard: respect. Changing after we look at results: adaptability. Everyone seeing the real picture: transparency. Building it together with users: collaboration. Match the behaviour to its anchor phrase and the distractors fall away.

blocks.text: If a stem mentions freedom to make decisions, the answer is empowerment, even when respect or transparency also sound positive.

explain.body: Empowerment fosters autonomy and self-management within teams (2.6.2).

test.q: A stem says a team has 'freedom to make decisions about its work'. Which characteristic of the agile mindset is being described?
test.why: Freedom to make decisions reflects autonomy and self-management, which is empowerment (2.6.2).

whyNot.0: Transparency is about open, rich information flow.
whyNot.2: Respect is about empathy and open-mindedness.
whyNot.3: Adaptability is about inspection and adaptation.

explain.body: Respect is rooted in empathy and open-mindedness: all voices are valued and diverse perspectives embraced (2.6.2).

test.q: Which behaviour best shows the agile characteristic of respect?
options: Letting the team choose its own tools
Changing the plan after a review
Making sure every member's view is heard
Putting the burn chart on a shared screen
test.why: Respect values all voices and embraces diverse perspectives (2.6.2).

whyNot.0: Choosing its own tools reflects empowerment.
whyNot.1: Changing course after review reflects adaptability.
whyNot.3: Showing the burn chart supports transparency.

explain.body: Adaptability reflects the agile values of inspection and adaptation in response to change (2.6.2).

test.q: After reviewing user feedback, a team changes the order of its next stories. Which characteristic of the agile mindset does this show?
test.why: Inspecting results and adapting in response is adaptability (2.6.2).

whyNot.1: Collaboration is about shared ownership and co-creation.
whyNot.2: Respect is about valuing all voices.
whyNot.3: Empowerment is about autonomy; the stem stresses changing after inspection.

explain.body: Transparency: open, rich information flow with visible work status, building trust and alignment. Collaboration: working closely with team, stakeholders and users, with shared ownership and co-creation (2.6.2).

test.q: Which phrase best describes the agile characteristic of collaboration?
options: Open information that is more than text
test.why: Collaboration creates a culture of shared ownership and mutual support that fosters co-created solutions (2.6.2).

whyNot.0: This describes transparency and rich communication.
